summary: The group is a mix of 28 analysis recipes on synthetic zones, tracts or rasters and 14 trajectory runs on the San Francisco vessel fleet. 16 of the 42 cards scrub a `Data:` knob, and four scrub by full rebuild (classCount, edgeDepth, resolution, sampleCount). The strongest pictures are trajectory-kalman, straight-line-catchments, drainage-network and points-in-polygons-choropleth. The weakest are resistance-connectivity (potential saturates to one colour and the wall cannot be seen), surface-preparation (the output covers the holes it filled), period-comparison and space-time-hot-spots (sparse cells with no geography), and the encounter trio, which shows a squashed fleet over an unlabelled bar chart. Several entries look the same: clock-encounters, trajectory-encounters and trajectory-closest-approach; zonal-distribution and points-in-polygons-choropleth; the two segregation recipes; the two resistance-connectivity recipes; zone-events and the two fleet-dwell recipes; track-similarity and track-similarity-search. Many cheap wins are spatial inputs that `update` already writes per frame: the zone rectangles (createZoneRectangles), the restriction box, the clock start, the encounter distance and the wall-gap conductances. Moving them under the pointer needs only a pointer-to-world value in update. Shared fixes would help many entries at once: lib/fleet.ts (the fleet fills about a third of the frame, and raiseFleet squeezes it further), lib/zones.ts (fixed zone centres, one of which no track visits), lib/tracts.ts and lib/quads.ts (no neighbour or member lookup for probing), and lib/earthquakes.ts (earthquake grids drawn with no geography). Fixed ranges are needed for the quantile fills.

sharedChanges.change: Fit the sampled vessel tracks to the frame (scale each axis separately to about 90% of the world) and drop or split tracks with long reporting gaps. Make raiseFleet keep the fleet's width while moving it up, so that the chart band does not halve the map.
Let createZoneRectangles take explicit centres, so that a pointer can move one zone per frame. Choose default centres where the fleet actually passes and stops: today the left zone receives no track.

Export a tract-at-point lookup (centres plus triangles) and the contiguity neighbour list for a hovered tract, plus a highlight overlay helper. Five tract recipes could then probe neighbours or kernels without changing the operations.

Add a zone-at-point lookup and an option on getQuadFill to outline one highlighted zone. Use a fixed `range` instead of auto for quantile and share outputs, so that changing the probability changes brightness.
Provide a context layer (coastline or the raw event dots sized by magnitude) in the same lattice transform. The three earthquake grids then read as places rather than as floating cells.
Expose the per-track positions in world space so that a hovered matrix cell can draw its two tracks over the matrix.

frameworkNeeds: pointer position in world coordinates (and the hovered element) passed to update(values) as a per-frame value, with no rebuild
glyphs drawn at the pointer: crosshair, ring of a world radius around an anchor, box outline, horizontal or vertical curtain line
render-only curtain (swipe) that clips one layer at pointer x against another
pointer-to-nearest lookups on CPU inputs: nearest node or dot, polygon or tract under the pointer, raster cell under the pointer, chart bar under the pointer
highlight overlay on polygons, segments and dots layers (one feature id or a small id list) without re-running the graph
read the value under the pointer from a GPU output that is already read back (addReadout buffers) for level-by-value bindings
discrete snapping with debounce, and a small cache of pre-built variants, for compile-time props (sampleCount, edgeDepth, source node, quarter)
chip readout that can show one scalar the operation computed (count, share, z) next to the bound prop
chart annotations: bar labels or ids, a reference line (observed value, zero), and bar hover mapped back to map features
